subject: HearthHealth VPC / On-prem hosting — discovery recap & asks
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lin <sara@hearthhealth.com>, Timothy Choi <timothy.choi@hearthhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: VPC / on-prem hosting — discovery call (HearthHealth)

Hi Sara / Tim —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment:

Goals / business drivers:
- Replace a latency-sensitive inference path currently hosted in AWS with closer on-prem model inference to meet HIPAA latency SLOs for clinician workflows.
- Ensure all PHI never leaves their network; storage must be on-prem with customer KMS and retained per 7-year retention policy.
- Maintain predictable cost-per-token for high-volume batch jobs (overnight transcription/embedding pipelines).

Constraints you raised:
- Strict data residency: models and inference logs must remain within the on-prem VLANs (no egress to public cloud for PHI).
- Air-gap for production environment: once validated, production should run without inbound internet access; approvals pending from Security.
- Network: limited outbound whitelisting; only a short list of IPs & ports will be allowed for control-plane telemetry. See your notes attached.

Open technical questions / asks from Redwood:
1) Can you share a network diagram that includes the CIDR ranges for the on-prem datacenter and any NAT/proxy appliances? (helps us size routing and control-plane connectivity)
2) Who is the Security approver for final airgap sign-off? Please provide contact + SOC2 evidence scope.
3) Are there any constraints on installing GPU drivers or container runtimes on the target hosts? (we can support common distros but need privilege to run the runtime)

Next steps proposed:
- Tim: if possible, share the network sketch + contact for security reviewer (today/tomorrow).
- Redwood: draft a minimal connectivity plan (control-plane whitelist & handshake flow) and an SOW estimate for a private delivery (we can propose Dedicated vs Private on-prem).
- Follow-up call: 30 minutes next week to review the connectivity plan and sample SOW.

Attachments: initial-network-notes.pdf (summary of our notes from the call)

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0132

From: Timothy Choi <timothy.choi@hearthhealth.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Sara Lin <sara@hearthhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: VPC / on-prem hosting — discovery call (HearthHealth)

Thanks Aditya — good summary.

Attaching the quick network sketch we drew post-call (hearthhealth-network-sketch.png). A few clarifications:
- Production inference will be on a pair of isolated racks in our Boston colocation (CIDRs: 10.100.0.0/22 and 10.100.4.0/22). We will not permit outbound internet from that VLAN except through a proxy appliance.
- For the initial pilot we can allow egress to a small set of IPs for control plane (certificate revocation and heartbeats). Security will require mTLS and client certs.
- Storage: model artifacts must be read-only from our internal NFS; secrets (KMS) are managed by our HSM; Redwood cannot hold plaintext keys.

Security reviewer is Sara Lin (cc'd) — she'll own SOC2 evidence review and airgap approval timeline.

We do need to confirm driver install privileges — our infra team can open a support window if Redwood provides a list of required kernel modules and driver versions.

Happy to jump on the follow-up next Wed 9/22 at 10am ET if that works — can we get an agenda and a short connectivity diagram from Redwood ahead of time?

Best,
Tim
CTO | HearthHealth
timothy.choi@hearthhealth.com

Marissa / Vivek —

Forwarding Tim's reply and the network sketch. Key takeaways for pricing & delivery:
- Air-gapped production with mTLS + client certs required; limited control-plane egress (we'll need to supply a short IP whitelist).
- KMS/HSM-managed keys; Redwood cannot store private keys—will need to support integration (bring-your-own-KMS pattern).
- Pilot footprint: 2 racks, GPU hosts (NVIDIA A100 equivalent), access to internal NFS for model artifacts.

Can you run a quick price + delivery assessment for: (A) Redwood Dedicated in their colocation with our private control-plane (we host control plane in their VPC via whitelisted IPs) and (B) True on-prem Private (we install runtime in their datacenter, zero egress for production, limited telemetry)?

Also need a short SOW draft we can share with Tim + Sara. I've put the HubSpot deal link below for reference.

Thanks — want to be ready to present options in the follow-up call (Wed 9/22).

Aditya

Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2027 11:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Recap: VPC / on-prem hosting — HearthHealth — pilot asks & security

Team —

Thanks for the context. Initial take:

Option A (Redwood Dedicated w/ private control plane):
- Pros: fastest to market, we retain control-plane features (monitoring/rollouts), limited on-prem work (whitelist & mTLS).
- Cons: requires limited egress; we'll need a signed whitelist agreement and SOC2 scoping.
- Ballpark pricing for 3-month pilot with A100-equivalent: $45k–$60k (fixed price + support); detailed quote pending infra sizing.

Option B (Redwood Private on-prem install):
- Pros: meets air-gap requirement fully (production zero egress), keys remain with customer, full control for HearthHealth.
- Cons: longer lead time (2–4 weeks for install + validation), increased eng/ops cost for privileged install; Ongoing support add-on recommended.
- Ballpark pricing for pilot: $80k–$120k (one-time install + 3 months of managed support).

I'll draft a short SOW and two pricing scenarios (A/B) and upload to the Drive folder. Also include a checklist for infra (kernel modules, driver versions, NFS mount steps). Expect a draft in ~24 hours.

If Tim & Sara want the pilot sooner, recommend going Dedicated first for the pilot, then transition to Private for production.

Marissa
Head of Solutions — Enterprise | Redwood Inference
